reaction: The lava provides a clearer route to an island.

reaction: The explanation that an island requires repeated eruptions was useful.
reason: The island is now available, but I don't yet know which bird-related object can reach it.

reaction: The island inspection resolved the route I had missed.
reason: The separated island population may develop different songs through inherited variation over generations.
expectation: Variation will produce a distinct island bird population or song.

effect: The island population now has distinct songs shaped by inherited variation and learning; the food-web goal remains.
reaction: It was useful to see that song differences can involve learning as well as inheritance.
reason: The established island birds and migrating flocks may now connect to the food web.
expectation: The food web will support the island birds and migrating flocks.

effect: Connecting the distinct songs to the food web completed the chapter's goal, linking island and migrating birds to larger communities.
reaction: The conclusion brought the separate migration, island and food-web threads together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Developing different island songs was most worthwhile: it showed that both inherited variation and learned traditions can contribute to differences between populations.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to connect seasonal journeys directly to the food web was the least useful action; the attempt gave no clue about the island route.

surprise.text: Seasonal journeys could not combine with the food web, but inspecting the island later revealed that the journeys could bring birds there.

arbitrary.text: Connecting different songs directly to the food web felt somewhat abstract: the result describes communities, but the songs themselves do not explain how the birds are supported.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: building the volcanic island and discovering how birds' songs could diverge combined satisfying connections with useful explanations.
